simple.meaning: חָטַם (châṭam) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to stop.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Isaiah, beginning at Isaiah 48:9. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָטַם (H2413) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: חָטַם (châṭam) / H2413 is traced through Isaiah 48:9 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H2413. chatam חָטַם verb hold in, restrain (Arabic strike the nose, attach the = camel-halter , noun muzzle, nose of beast ; Late Hebrew חֲטָם nose-ring of camel , חוֺטָם ; Aramaic חוּטְמָא nose ; compare חטם , Inscription Zinjirli; according to DHM Sendsch. 34, of taming wild beasts ) — Qal Imperfect ׃ הַכְרִיֶתךָ לְבִלְתִּי אֶחֱטָםלָֿ֑ךְ Isa 48:9 I will restrain for thee (mine anger), not to cut thee off (|| אַמִּי אַאֲרִיךְ ).
